A common myth about Albert Einstein!

There is a persistent legend that Einstein failed mathematics in school, but this is largely an exaggeration or even a complete fabrication. While it's true that Einstein was not always the best student and struggled with certain subjects, there is no credible evidence to suggest he ever failed math.

In fact, Einstein's interest in mathematics began at a young age. He was fascinated by geometry and developed his own theories about space and time. By the time he was 16, he had already devoured Euclid's "Elements" and was experimenting with mathematical concepts that would later become the foundation of his groundbreaking work.

Einstein's academic report cards show that he excelled in mathematics throughout his school years. In a letter to a friend in 1895, Einstein wrote: "I have disposed of all my earlier difficulties in arithmetic and I am now able to grasp even the most difficult mathematical concepts."

It's worth noting that Einstein did leave school at the age of 16 due to his father's health issues and family financial struggles. He then pursued a degree in physics from the Swiss Federal Polytechnic University, where he excelled in mathematics and went on to develop his famous theory of relativity.

So, while Einstein may have had his share of struggles with certain subjects, there is no evidence to suggest that math was one of them.
